Physical results, unexpected behaviour and its interpretation, comparisons
with literature, and choices of approximation. Entries are dated H2 sections;
existing entries are never edited.

## 2026-11-05: Validation strategy for the first milestones

The first two milestones are deliberately free of self-consistency. Milestone
1a, the empty lattice, has an exact answer: the folded free-electron
parabolas $\tfrac12|\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{G}|^2$. With the k-dependent
kinetic-energy cutoff proposed in the
[theory post](../theory/01a_empty_lattice.qmd), every eigenvalue below the
cutoff is exact and none is missing. That allows a strong test: a wrong
reciprocal lattice, a missing plane wave or a padding component leaking into
the spectrum shows up as an error of order one in units of
$\tfrac12(2\pi/a)^2$, against a tolerance of $10^{-10}$ Ha.

The empty lattice cannot detect errors that only matter when plane waves
couple, such as the sign convention of the structure factor or the
indexing of $V(\mathbf{G}-\mathbf{G}')$. That is Milestone 1b's job, validated
against published Cohen–Bergstresser silicon bands.

## 2026-11-05: Empty-lattice bands reproduced

The fcc empty-lattice band structure ([validation](../validation/01a_empty_lattice.qmd))
matches the folded free-electron parabolas at every k-point on L–Γ–X–U|K–Γ,
with no plane wave below the cutoff missing. The degeneracies at all six
high-symmetry points match the hand-derived table. That includes W, which the
plotted path never visits.

Two points of interpretation. First, the agreement with the library's own
analytic reference is exact, not merely within tolerance. For a diagonal
Hamiltonian that is expected and says little. The meaningful comparison is in
the acceptance tests, against an independent enumeration. Second, the U|K
equivalence shows up as continuity of the band energies across the path
break. Only the slopes change, because the path direction does.

Nothing here tests the coupling between plane waves, where the physically
interesting errors live (structure-factor sign, the 1/Ω normalisation of
Ṽ(G − G′)). The property tests do exercise a non-diagonal, test-only coupling
term, and it agrees with an independent NumPy diagonalisation. Milestone 1b,
with Cohen–Bergstresser silicon, is the first physical test of that path.

## 2026-11-05: Band sticking in diamond silicon is on the X–W line, not the whole face

While reviewing the 1b theory post, the reviewer found that in the
Cohen–Bergstresser model the bands stay paired from X to W along
$\tfrac{2\pi}{a}(0,1,z)$. The reviewer generalised this to the entire square
face of the Brillouin zone. A throwaway check refutes the generalisation. At a
generic face point, $\tfrac{2\pi}{a}(0.13, 1, 0.21)$, the levels are split by
several mHa, while along X–W they pair to rounding. The pairing needs the
non-symmorphic operation of the diamond space group (with a phase of −1 on the
face) *together with* time reversal, and that combination holds on the X–W
line. The acceptance tests therefore sample that line and include the generic
face point as a negative control. The pairing should disappear once spin–orbit
coupling is added.

A second point from the review: the 1966 paper's exactly diagonalised basis
(about 15 plane waves) is far from converged, with the indirect gap off by
roughly a factor of two. Its published values are nevertheless close to the
converged model, which credits the Löwdin second-order correction. The
validation document will show this from the library.

## 2026-11-05: Cohen–Bergstresser silicon reproduced

The [1b validation](../validation/01b_cohen_bergstresser.qmd) shows that all
seven Si splittings in Table I of Cohen & Bergstresser (1966) are reproduced
within the tolerances derived from the paper's own rounding and stated
convergence. The worst entry is Γ₂₅′–Γ₂′. The paper identifies Γ₂′ as the
level most sensitive to the form factors, so its 0.1 eV rounding and
second-order basis treatment matter most there.

Diagonalising exactly in the paper's explicitly treated basis (about 15 plane
waves) gives an indirect gap of roughly half the converged value. The
published numbers sit much closer to the converged model than to that basis.
This is quantitative evidence that their Löwdin correction was accurate, not
just a small adjustment.

Physically the model gives the textbook picture: the indirect gap with its
minimum near 0.85 X, Γ₁₅ below Γ₂′, bands paired along X–W, and the L
parities that explain the "surprising" L₂′-below-L₁ ordering. Its gap is
about 0.3 eV below experiment, a known limitation of a three-parameter local
model. That limitation motivates the norm-conserving pseudopotentials and
self-consistency of the next milestone.

One numerical subtlety worth remembering: a band structure cannot distinguish
H from conj(H), so it cannot tell a crystal from its inversion image. The
convention ⟨G|V|G′⟩ = Ṽ(G − G′) and the structure-factor sign are therefore
pinned by real-space and matrix-element tests rather than by any band energy.
That will matter as soon as positions get forces.
